messages:
Alex K.: FYI saw a CPU-side perf regression after the kernel-selection tweak landed. Small requests (<=64 tokens) 20-30% higher 95th. Perf traces attached.
benchbot: nsys run uploaded: https://bench.redwood/nsys/1967890123 — perfetto link: https://perfetto.app/trace/1967890123 :eyes:
Maria P.: quick look — flame shows big rust::tokenizer::tokenize_batch hot path + scheduler wakeups in batcher.poll. Also a lot of 'PyThreadState_Get' and libc memcpy.
Ryan C.: could KV cache evictions be increasing tokenization frequency? Any correlation with prefix hits?
Alex K.: checked — no evictions. KV-hit rate unchanged. This looks like scheduler churn & Python overhead when batch size=1.
Sam V.: attached commands I ran:
```
perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid> -- sleep 30
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
result: deep Python stacks from tokenize_batch -> PyObject_Call -> tokenize_one
Jess L.: I pushed a small repro that toggles kernel selection heuristics: fallback to single-kernel path reduces overhead by ~12% but increases GPU time slightly. Tradeoff?
Maria P.: hypothesis: kernel-selection adds sync points for quick paths, causing scheduler to wake frequently. Need to avoid kernel rebind for short sequences.
Ryan C.: can we add a cheap fast-path: if seq_len <= 64 and batch_size <= 2, skip kernel metadata checks and use cached kernel id? microbench suggests win.
Alex K.: agree. I'll prototype cached-kernel fast-path and add a metric to count fast-path hits. Also add perf trace switch (env REDWOOD_PERF=1) to include perf markers.
Sam V.: sounds good. Next steps: Alex to prod a patch, Maria to validate perf traces, Jess to run perf regression harness. :thumbsup:
Jess L.: I'll also add a small unit test that asserts no extra Python frames are introduced for the fast-path.
benchbot: deployment scheduled to canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC — runbook: /runbooks/perf-kernel-fastpath
Alex K.: thanks everyone — saving traces to shared folder: https://files.redwood/tmp/1967890123-traces.tar.gz
